claim: CGEL classifies the four deictic temporal nouns as pronouns on the strength of their inability to take determiners. It then adduces their deictic meaning.
evidence_summary: Compare today with quantificational plenty in plenty of time. CGEL says this use of plenty permits no determiner or modifier (p. 350), yet treats it as nominal outside the pronoun subclass.
finding: Exclusion is shared by noun uses on opposite sides of the proposed boundary. Its presence alone cannot identify a pronoun. Deixis remains positive evidence of resemblance, and the genitive contrast bears on the comparison with prepositions.
inference: Does the inability to take determiners distinguish temporal pronouns from all other nominal uses?

evidence.passage: §10.1.4, p. 429, final paragraph. Yesterday, today, tonight and tomorrow belong to the pronoun subclass “by virtue of their inability to take determiners”. CGEL then adduces deixis and compares their genitives with now and then.
evidence.example: The linked manuscript develops a related analysis. See the working-note record for the test applied to this CGEL passage.
evidence.establishes: Related work by the catalogue’s author. Its inclusion provides background rather than independent corroboration.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
